Cancer Basemap is public, aggregate cancer data keyed on geography and time,
published as monthly Parquet releases that you can query from DuckDB, R,
Python or a browser. There is no account and no token, and every release
stays attached to the numbers it produced.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# Build-time stats strip. Everything printed here is read from the latest
# release over HTTPS (manifest.json, then read_parquet on the paths it lists)
# plus the two places releases are published; nothing is typed by hand.
import json
import re
import urllib.request

import duckdb

BASE = "https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/"


def get_json(url):
    # Cloudflare answers urllib's default User-Agent with a 403.
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "cancerbasemap-docs"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.load(r)


manifest = get_json(BASE + "manifest.json")
paths = {f"{t['schema']}.{t['table']}": BASE + t["path"] for t in manifest["tables"]}
con = duckdb.connect()


def scalar(sql):
    return con.execute(sql).fetchone()[0]


def parquet(table):
    return f"read_parquet('{paths[table]}')"


obs = parquet("measure.observation")
sources = scalar(f"SELECT count(DISTINCT source) FROM {obs}")
measures = scalar(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {parquet('measure.definition')}")
# Filtering on the geo_id prefix keeps these scans cheap; they count distinct
# ids across boundary vintages, so Connecticut's old counties and new planning
# regions both appear.
counties, tracts, editions = con.execute(f"""
    SELECT count(DISTINCT geo_id) FILTER (WHERE geo_id LIKE 'county:%'),
           count(DISTINCT geo_id) FILTER (WHERE geo_id LIKE 'tract:%'),
           count(DISTINCT (source, source_release))
    FROM {obs}
""").fetchone()
tables = len(manifest["tables"])
rows = sum(t["row_count"] or 0 for t in manifest["tables"])
size_gb = sum(t["bytes"] or 0 for t in manifest["tables"]) / 1e9

# A release is published once on R2 (dated folder) and once on Hugging Face
# (tag of the same date); count each date once.
r2_dates = {d[:-1] for d in get_json("https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/")["directories"]
            if re.fullmatch(r"v\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/", d)}
hf_dates = {t["name"] for t in get_json("https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/seandavis/cancerbasemap/refs")["tags"]
            if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", t["name"])}
releases = len(r2_dates | {"v" + d for d in hf_dates})

cards = [
    (manifest["release"], "release date"),
    (sources, "sources with observations"),
    (f"{tables} / {rows / 1e6:.1f}M", "tables / total rows, all schemas"),
    (f"{size_gb:.1f} GB", "whole bundle, as Parquet"),
    (measures, "measures defined"),
    (f"{counties:,}", "county IDs with an observation"),
    (f"{tracts:,}", "tract IDs with an observation"),
    # Every edition a source has published stays in the release beside the next one, so a
    # change between editions can be traced; that is the history this page counts.
    (f"{editions:,}", "source editions kept side by side"),
]
# Only the releases that ship a catchment.center table get this card.
if "catchment.center" in paths:
    centers = scalar(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {parquet('catchment.center')}")
    cards.append((centers, "cancer centers with catchments"))
cards.append((releases, "releases published"))

print(f"**As of release {manifest['release']}**\n")
# Three across when the cards divide evenly by three, else four, so the last row is never a stray card.
span = 4 if len(cards) % 3 == 0 else 3
print("::: {.grid .mt-2 .mb-5}\n")
for value, caption in cards:
    print(f"::: {{.g-col-6 .g-col-md-{span} .card .p-3 .stat}}\n"
          f"<span class='stat-number'>{value}</span>\n"
          f"<span class='small text-muted'>{caption}</span>\n:::\n")
print(":::")
```

## Why I built it

Cancer Basemap is a thin layer. It takes public cancer numbers from several
sources and delivers them versioned, joinable and citable, keyed on geography
and time, so that a county or tract means the same thing in every table and a
number stays attached to the release it came from.

The sources are ones many of us already use. [State Cancer
Profiles](https://statecancerprofiles.cancer.gov/) is where most people look
up incidence and mortality, [PLACES](https://www.cdc.gov/places/) publishes
small-area prevalence through its own portal, and [Cancer
InFocus](concepts/cancer-infocus.qmd) packages catchment data for the
NCI-designated centers. This layer draws on the first two and sits beside the
third.

I started from a small need. A cancer center writing a CCSG or COE report
wants one sentence it can defend: *in our catchment, as reported by source S
in release R, the measure was X.* The sentence is easy to write. The number
behind it can come from a screenshot, or a CSV downloaded some months ago and
never dated, and keeping the source and release beside each value is what
this layer is for. It is a starting point, and I would like to hear where it
falls short for you.

## What you can do with it

::: {.grid .mt-2}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### A catchment burden table {.mt-0}

Build the county table a CCSG or COE report asks for, with the source and
release beside every value: the [catchment report
recipe](recipes/catchment-report.qmd).
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Where screening lags {.mt-0}

Rank a state's counties on screening and put rurality next to them in
[Screening in a state's counties](recipes/screening-rurality.qmd).
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### What changed between releases {.mt-0}

Compare [PLACES 2024 with 2025](recipes/places-diff.qmd) or [State Cancer
Profiles across vintages](recipes/scp-vintages.qmd), county by county, so a
shift in a number can be traced to a shift in the source.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Suppression, kept visible {.mt-0}

A suppressed cell is a status with a NULL value, never a zero. [Suppressed
and unavailable cells](recipes/suppressed-cells.qmd) shows how to count them
and keep them out of your averages.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Environmental context {.mt-0}

EJScreen, AirToxScreen, radon zones and public water systems sit in the same
bundle as the screening and incidence tables. The
[Dictionary](dictionary/index.qmd) lists each table and column.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Build on it {.mt-0}

[Catchment Profiles](https://seandavi.github.io/catchment-profiles/) is an
independent open-source app built only on the public releases.
:::

:::

## Live county map

The map below reads a small, versioned extract of `measure.observation`
written at *build* time — the same numbers you'd get querying the release
directly, just not re-queried on every page load. ["Run this live in your
browser"](recipes/screening-rurality.qmd) runs the same measure/release
query against the real, 29.6-million-row table through DuckDB-WASM — scoped to
one state at a time rather than the whole country, for the reason given on
that page.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# Build-time extract: ~6 cancer-relevant PLACES county measures, releases
# 2024 and 2025, written to extracts/home_map.json for the {ojs} map below to
# read. This is real release output, not a fixture — if a release changes
# these numbers, the next render of this page changes too.
import json

import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS cbm (READ_ONLY)")

MEASURES = [
    "PLACES:CANCER:age_adjusted",
    "PLACES:COLON_SCREEN:age_adjusted",
    "PLACES:MAMMOUSE:age_adjusted",
    "PLACES:CSMOKING:age_adjusted",
    "PLACES:OBESITY:age_adjusted",
    "PLACES:CHECKUP:age_adjusted",
]
RELEASES = ["2024", "2025"]
# Short codes keep the JSON small (~1.1 MB uncompressed for 6 measures x 2
# releases x ~3,222 counties) — see value_status meaning on the Concepts >
# Suppression page.
STATUS_CODE = {
    "reported": "R",
    "suppressed_small_count": "S",
    "suppressed_complementary": "C",
    "suppressed_reliability": "U",
    "not_available": "N",
    "not_applicable": "X",
}

placeholders = ",".join(f"'{m}'" for m in MEASURES)
rows = con.sql(f"""
    SELECT source_release, measure_id, geo_id, value, lower, upper, value_status
    FROM cbm.measure.observation
    WHERE source = 'PLACES' AND source_release IN ('2024', '2025')
      AND measure_id IN ({placeholders})
      AND geo_id LIKE 'county:%' AND stratum_id = 'PLACES:ALL'
     
""").fetchall()

obs = {}
for release, measure_id, geo_id, value, lower, upper, status in rows:
    fips = geo_id.split(":", 1)[1]
    obs.setdefault(release, {}).setdefault(measure_id, []).append([
        fips,
        round(value, 1) if value is not None else None,
        round(lower, 1) if lower is not None else None,
        round(upper, 1) if upper is not None else None,
        STATUS_CODE.get(status, "?"),
    ])

labels = dict(con.sql(f"""
    SELECT measure_id, label FROM cbm.measure.definition
    WHERE measure_id IN ({placeholders})
""").fetchall())

counties = dict(con.sql("""
    SELECT fips, name FROM cbm.geography.unit
    WHERE level = 'county' AND vintage = 2026
""").fetchall())

payload = {
    "measures": [{"id": m, "label": labels.get(m, m)} for m in MEASURES],
    "releases": RELEASES,
    "counties": counties,
    "obs": obs,
}

import os
os.makedirs("extracts", exist_ok=True)
with open("extracts/home_map.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(payload, f, separators=(",", ":"))
print(f"wrote extracts/home_map.json: {len(rows)} rows, "
      f"{os.path.getsize('extracts/home_map.json') / 1024:.0f} KB")
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Two known gaps in this map, verified against the data:**

- **Connecticut** doesn't join. PLACES 2024/2025 report Connecticut's nine
  2022-vintage planning regions; the county boundary shapes used to draw
  this map (`us-atlas`, still on legacy county lines) only have the eight
  counties those regions replaced. Connecticut draws as no-data here — a
  boundary-vintage mismatch worth surfacing, not a bug to hide (see
  [Concepts › Boundary vintages](concepts/boundaries.qmd)).
- **Kentucky and Pennsylvania** show only 2 of these 6 measures for release
  2025 — mammography use and colorectal cancer screening — with cancer
  (non-skin)/melanoma, current smoking, obesity, and annual checkup all
  missing. Verified directly against `raw.places__county`: both states
  report 40 distinct measures for 2024 but only 5 for 2025 (PLACES-wide,
  not specific to this map's 6), and CDC's own [PLACES release
  notes](https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/index.html)
  confirm why — "Estimates for Kentucky and Pennsylvania were not available
  for measures based on the 2023 BRFSS. However, the five measures based on
  the 2022 BRFSS were carried over for Kentucky and Pennsylvania" (mammography
  use, colorectal cancer screening, dental visits, short sleep duration, and
  all teeth lost — only the first two are among this map's 6) — the two
  states did not collect enough months of 2023 BRFSS data to meet PLACES'
  own inclusion threshold, so those five measures are simply carried forward
  from the prior data year rather than missing.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mapData = FileAttachment("extracts/home_map.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof measureId = Inputs.select(mapData.measures, {
  label: "Measure",
  format: (d) => d.label,
  value: mapData.measures[0]
})
viewof release = Inputs.select(mapData.releases, { label: "Release" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
STATUS_LABEL = ({
  R: "reported", S: "suppressed (small count)", C: "suppressed (complementary)",
  U: "suppressed (unreliable)", N: "not available", X: "not applicable"
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rowsForSelection = mapData.obs[release]?.[measureId.id] ?? []
byFips = new Map(rowsForSelection.map((r) => [r[0], r]))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// County boundaries live nowhere in a release (it holds tabular data, not
// geometry) — loaded once, at view time, from a public TopoJSON CDN.
countyGeo = {
  const topojsonMod = await import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/topojson-client@3/+esm");
  const us = await fetch("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/us-atlas@3/counties-10m.json").then((r) => r.json());
  return topojsonMod.feature(us, us.objects.counties);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
joined = countyGeo.features.map((f) => {
  const row = byFips.get(f.id);
  const name = mapData.counties[f.id] ?? f.properties.name;
  return { ...f, properties: { ...f.properties, fips: f.id, name, row } };
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  projection: "albers-usa",
  color: {
    type: "sequential",
    scheme: "blues",
    label: measureId.label,
    legend: true,
    nice: true
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.geo(joined, {
      fill: (d) => (d.properties.row && d.properties.row[4] === "R") ? d.properties.row[1] : null,
      stroke: "white",
      strokeWidth: 0.3,
      title: (d) => {
        const row = d.properties.row;
        if (!row) return `${d.properties.name} (${d.properties.fips}): no data`;
        if (row[4] !== "R")
          return `${d.properties.name} (${d.properties.fips}): ${STATUS_LABEL[row[4]]} — no value`;
        return `${d.properties.name} (${d.properties.fips})\n${measureId.label}: ${row[1]}% (CI ${row[2]}–${row[3]})\nrelease ${release}`;
      }
    }),
    // Suppressed, unavailable, or unmatched counties: drawn grey, never left
    // to read as zero (AGENTS.md's suppression gate applies to how the map
    // draws, not only to the value column).
    Plot.geo(
      joined.filter((d) => !d.properties.row || d.properties.row[4] !== "R"),
      { fill: "#ddd", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.3, fillOpacity: 0.6 }
    )
  ],
  width: 900,
  height: 550
})
```

## Where next

[Start here](start/index.qmd) has the ATTACH statement and the way in for R,
SAS, SEER\*Stat, Python and the DuckDB CLI. The [Playground](playground.qmd)
runs SQL against the latest release in your browser, the
[Recipes](recipes/index.qmd) work through whole questions, and the
[Dictionary](dictionary/index.qmd) lists every table and measure.
[Releases](releases.qmd) and [Versions and
citation](guides/versions-and-citation.qmd) say which version to pin and how
to cite it. [Catchment Profiles](https://seandavi.github.io/catchment-profiles/)
shows what an app on top of this looks like.

Some sources are still waiting on a licence review and are not in the
bundle yet, new releases arrive monthly, and catchment boundaries for more
centers are on the way. If you need a source or a center that is missing, [open
an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-basemap/issues) and
say what you are trying to report.
